definitions.explanation: Rebuilding a physical structure such as a building or temple that has been destroyed or damaged.

definitions.gloss: reorganization, restructuring, getting back on one's feet
definitions.explanation: Rebuilding or restructuring something abstract such as a business, finances, or one's life after a setback.

examples.japanese: {寺|てら}を{再建|さいけん}した。
{火事|かじ}で{焼|や}けた{城|しろ}は{十|じゅう}{年|ねん}かけて{再建|さいけん}された。
examples.english: The castle that burned down in a fire was rebuilt over ten years.

examples.japanese: {被災|ひさい}{地|ち}の{住宅|じゅうたく}{再建|さいけん}が{急|いそ}がれている。
examples.english: Housing reconstruction in the disaster-affected area is being urgently pursued.

examples.japanese: {経営|けいえい}を{再建|さいけん}する。
{財政|ざいせい}{再建|さいけん}が{急務|きゅうむ}だ。
examples.english: Financial restructuring is an urgent task.

examples.japanese: {倒産|とうさん}した{会社|かいしゃ}を{再建|さいけん}するために{新|あたら}しい{経営|けいえい}{陣|じん}が{招|まね}かれた。
examples.english: A new management team was brought in to restructure the bankrupt company.

notes:
Compound of {再|さい} (again) + {建|けん} (to build). Covers both physical rebuilding and figurative restructuring.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{再建|さいけん}する (to rebuild, to restructure)
・{経営|けいえい}{再建|さいけん} (business restructuring)
・{財政|ざいせい}{再建|さいけん} (fiscal restructuring)
・{生活|せいかつ}の{再建|さいけん} (rebuilding one's life)
・{再建|さいけん}{計画|けいかく} (reconstruction plan)

DISTINCTIONS:
・{再建|さいけん}: rebuilding something that was lost or destroyed; implies restoring to a former state
・{建|た}て{替|か}え: rebuilding by demolishing the old and constructing anew (not after destruction)
・{復興|ふっこう}: recovery and revitalization on a larger scale (of a region or nation)

cross_references.notes: 債権 means a claim or bond (financial) — same reading, different meaning
